ARC-REV-01.rationale: Branch lookup (Catalog.findBranch), copies at a branch (Catalog.copiesAt) and queue order (Holds.queueFor) are all asked of Tier 2. The one exception is a copy's status (on loan vs on shelf): the Tier 3 report derives it inline by looking the copy up in the Loans map instead of asking a Tier 1/2 status function. That re-derives part of the copy-state rule in Tier 3. It does not contradict any existing rule visible in the diff, so 1 rather than 0.

ARC-REV-02.rationale: All new file output goes through the existing Files port, and state is read through ports.Store.Load. The change also removes `open System.IO` and the direct File.WriteAllLines call from Tier 3, an existing violation it touched. No new effect is added below Tier 4. The CLI only dispatches to Tier 3 use cases and renders view models.

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The inventory report restates how a copy's status is derived (loan present means on loan, otherwise on shelf) instead of using one shared status derivation. The existing `shelf` command renders the same 'on shelf' status (seen in tests). The member CSV layout is also restated as a literal header, separate from the format that import-members parses. These copies currently agree (the round-trip test passes), so 1 rather than 0.

ARC-REV-01.rationale: import-copies leaves every validity decision (duplicate copy, unknown book, branch placement) to Tier 2 Catalog.addCopy and Catalog.findBranch. Tier 3 only parses the file, numbers lines and coordinates the all-or-nothing commit. The new held-copy status, however, extends the Tier 3 inline status derivation: Tier 3 decides that a shelved copy whose book has a non-empty queue is 'held'. The queue itself comes from Tier 2 (Holds.queueFor), so this re-derives part of the rule without contradicting it.

ARC-REV-02.rationale: The file read goes through the existing Files port, an unreadable file is an explicit None mapped to an error, and persistence uses the existing commit or Store path. The fold over rows is pure, applied to the loaded library before commit. No effect is added in Tier 1/2. The CLI change only dispatches to the use case. The direct JsonFileStore use in `backup` is existing code and not part of this change.

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The number of holds is taken from the authoritative Tier 2 queue (Holds.queueFor), and copy validity and branch placement come from Catalog.addCopy, so this change introduces no new copy of a domain fact. The 'on shelf' literal it keeps belongs to the status derivation already counted in change set 1, which this change neither duplicates further nor contradicts.
